711.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Raag Todi, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Without the Lord my mind cannot live. When the Guru unites (me) with the Lord God, my beloved, my breath of life, there is no more going round in the world-ocean. A longing for God has taken hold of my heart, that with my eyes I may behold the Lord, the Lord God. The merciful True Guru has made the Lord's Name firm (within me): (the Name of) the Lord is the level road to the Lord God. I have found the Name of God, the Lord of countless hues, the Name of the Lord Govind, the Lord God; the Lord has come to taste sweet in my heart, my mind and my body; a good fortune (shines) on my face and forehead. Those whose minds cling to greed and the vices have forgotten the Lord, the Being most good; they are called manmukhs (the self-willed), foolish and ignorant, and an evil fortune is on their foreheads. From the True Guru (I) have received an intellect that discerns, the Guru's wisdom, which is of God, the Great. Servant Nanak has received the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) from the Guru: the fortune written on (his) forehead from the beginning (has come to light). ॥4॥
711.2: Raag Todi, Ghar 1, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Sants have known no one else; carefree, they stay ever in the Lord's love, they whose side the Master takes. High is your canopy, O Master; no one else has spread (one like it). Such an undying (Lord) have the devotees found; the wise remain absorbed in (his) love. Disease and grief, pain, old age and death do not come near the Lord's servant. They remain fearless, their attention on the One; O Nanak, (their) mind has come to rest in the Lord. ॥2॥
Dupade (du, two; pad, stanza): hymns of two stanzas.
711.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Forgetting the Lord, there is ever ruin. How can deception touch the one who has your shelter? Whatever life is lived without Simran (remembrance of God) is a burning, like the long life of a snake. Though (one) reign over the nine regions (of the world), at the last he will depart a loser. The praises of the treasure of virtues have been sung only by the one on whom (he) has shown his grace; that one is at peace, blessed is his birth; Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥2॥
712.1: Raag Todi, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O mind, (the mortal) has run about, run off in the ten directions, absorbed in Maya, lured by its taste and by greed: God himself has led (him) astray. Not for a moment has he fixed this mind on the Lord's story, the Lord's praise, the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy); he delights at the sight of the safflower's colour, and goes off to peer into others' homes. He has not loved the lotus feet, nor won the favour of the True Being (the Guru); (such ones) run in many ways after what is running away, as the oilman's ox is driven round and round. He has not practised the Naam, giving and bathing, nor sung (the Lord's) praise for an instant; attaching (it) to many falsehoods, he has kept the mind pleased, and has not understood what is (truly) his own. He has never done good to others, nor served the True Guru and meditated (on the Lord); mixing with the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride), in their company and their talk, he is drunk on the wine of Maya. I make my prayer in the Saadh Sangat: hearing (that you are) the Lord who loves devotion, I have come. Nanak has run to the Lord's shelter: keep (my) honour, making (me) your own. ॥5॥
Chaupade (chau, four; pad, stanza): hymns of four stanzas.
Kasumbh, the safflower, gives a bright dye that soon fades.
712.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without understanding, the human being has come (into the world) in vain. He makes many adornments and decorations, like a corpse being dressed. The miser has run and run and toiled, and gathered Maya; (with it) no giving, no merit, no service of the Sants: it has been of no use at all. Putting on her jewels, the woman decked the bed and made a fine display; (but) she did not gain her husband's company, and looking (at it all) again and again she was in pain. All day long he works for hire, pounding husks with a pestle; toil is all he gets, like one doing forced labour: it is of no use to his own home. The one on whom God's grace has come has made the Naam dwell in his heart; he has taken the shelter of the Saadh Sangat; O servant Nanak, he has found the Lord's sweet essence. ॥4॥
712.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O treasure of mercy, O Lord, dwell in (my) heart always. Kindle in (me) such understanding that love for God may take hold (of me). May I obtain the dust (of the feet) of your servant, and taking it again and again, apply it to my forehead. (By it) one is made pure from being a great sinner; (may) I sing the Lord's Kirtan (songs of God's praise) and his virtues. May your command taste sweet to me; may what you do please me. Whatever you give, with that may this (mind) be satisfied; may I run nowhere else. May I know you, God, my Master, ever near; one should live as the dust of all. When the company of the holy is gained, then one finds one's own God. For ever and ever we are your little ones; you, God, are our sovereign. Nanak is (your) child, you are (his) mother and father; your Name in (his) mouth is (his) milk. ॥4॥
713.1: Raag Todi, Ghar 2, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I beg the gift of the Name, O Master. Nothing else will go with me; (may I) by your grace receive the singing of your praises. Rule, riches and many pleasures and delights: all are the shade of a tree. Running and running, (the mortal) runs about in many ways, (yet) all his deeds are of no avail. If I want anything else but Govind, all (of it) is seen to be unripe. Says Nanak, I beg the dust (of the feet) of the Sants, (so that) my mind may find rest. ॥2॥
713.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Name of dear God is the support of the mind. It is the life, the breath and the peace of this mind; it is what I have to live by. The Naam is (my) caste, the Naam is my honour, the Naam is my family. The Naam is a companion, ever at my side; the Lord's Name carries me across. Pleasures of the senses are spoken of as many, (yet) none of them goes along. The Naam is Nanak's beloved friend; what lies in my treasury is the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
713.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Sing the sublime praises (of the Lord), and the diseases are wiped away; the face becomes bright, the mind becomes pure, and your world here and hereafter is kept safe. Washing (his) feet, I serve the Guru, and offer my mind (to him) as the offering. Give up selfhood, strife and pride, and accept whatever comes to be. He alone is set to the service of the Sants on whose forehead (that) writ is written. Says Nanak, apart from the One there is no other able to do (anything). ॥2॥
713.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O True Guru, I have come to your shelter. May I receive peace, the Lord's Name and honour; take away my anxiety. No other resting place comes to mind; worn out, I have fallen at your door. Set aside the account (of my deeds); only without an account can we be freed; save us, the worthless. Ever forgiving, ever merciful, (he) gives support to all. Servant Nanak has taken the shelter of the Sant (the Guru): save (me) this time. ॥2॥
713.5: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Singing with the tongue the praises of Gopal, the treasure (of virtues), peace, Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and joy well up in the mind, and all sorrows flee. Whatever they ask for, that very thing they receive, serving the feet of the Lord, the home of every delight; they are freed from both birth and death, and cross the terrifying world-ocean. Searching and searching, the servants have reflected on the essence, and hold to Govind alone. If you want lasting well-being, O Nanak, remember Narayan for ever. ॥2॥
714.1: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). By the Guru's grace the slanderer has been driven off. The Supreme Lord God became merciful, and with the arrow of Shiv (the Lord, the source of good) cut off (his) head. Death, its net and Jam (the messenger of Death) cannot (even) look at (me): (I) have taken the path of Truth. Eating and spending, nothing runs short: (I) have earned the wealth of the jewel of (the Name of) Ram. Within an instant (the slanderer) turned to ashes: he reaped what he himself had done. Servant Nanak speaks (the word of) the scriptures, Agam and Nigam; all the world sees it all. ॥2॥
714.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O miser, (your) body and mind are full of sins. In the Saadh Sangat meditate on the Master: the One Lord alone (can) cover (them). The ship has many holes bursting open, and they cannot be stopped (by hand). (If one) worships the One whose ship it is, in his company the counterfeit become genuine. (The mortal) wants to lift mountains with talk, (but) they stay lying where they are. Nanak has neither strength nor any power; O God, keep (us): we have fallen at your shelter. ॥2॥
714.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In my mind I meditate on the lotus feet of the Lord. The Lord's Name is the medicine: an axe that cuts out (the ills of) bile and wind and destroys them. (It) dispels the three fevers, destroys pain, and is a store of peace. No obstacle touches the one whose prayer is before God. By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), Narayan is the physician, God the One, the Cause of causes. (To those of) a child's mind (he) is the perfect Giver of peace; Nanak's support is the Lord, Har Har. ॥2॥

Pitt and baat (bile and wind): two of the three humours of Indian medicine, held to cause disease when they are out of balance. The three fevers: adhi (ills of the mind), biadhi (ills of the body) and upadhi (troubles and calamities that come from without).
714.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, for ever and ever. Showing his grace, the Master, the Supreme Lord, has himself made (the heart's deserted town) inhabited again. He whose (servants) they were has himself taken care of them again, and sorrow and anguish have perished. Giving his hand, (he) has protected his servants; the Lord has become (their) mother and father. Every being and creature has become kind, (since) the Lord, the Master, has shown mercy. Nanak has fallen at the shelter of the Destroyer of pain, whose glory is great. ॥2॥
714.5: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Master, I have come to your shelter, to your court. O Giver who destroys millions of offences, who but you can save (me)? Searching and searching in many ways, I have reflected on all things: in the Saadh Sangat the supreme state is attained; caught up in Maya, in its bonds, (people) lose (the game of life). Love for the lotus feet has taken hold of (my) mind, (since) the beloved godly ones have met (me). Nanak rejoices, repeating the Lord (again and again), and has rid (himself) of all diseases. ॥2॥
715.1: Raag Todi, Ghar 3, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Yes, yes, O fool, you are clinging (to it), and not a little; what is not yours, that you have taken for your own. You have not recognised your own Ram for even an instant; what is another's, that you have believed to be yours. The Naam is (your) companion: that you have not made to dwell in the mind; you have fixed your attention on what will leave (you). You have hoarded that by which (you stay) hungry and thirsty; the Amrit (life-giving) Naam you have not taken as provisions (for the journey). (You) have fallen into the well of lust, anger and attachment; by the Guru's grace, O Nanak, (only) some rare one has crossed over. ॥4॥
715.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Within me there is the One alone, the Lord, the Lord; I have made acquaintance with no other. By great fortune I have found my Guru; the Guru has made the Lord's Name firm within me. The Lord, Har Har, is (my) chanting and austerity, (my) fasts and observances; meditating on the Lord, Har Har, (I have) every comfort and well-being. (My) conduct, (my) dealings and (my) caste are the Lord's praises; hearing the Lord's Kirtan, (there is) supreme bliss. Says Nanak, the one who has found the Master: everything has come into his house. ॥4॥
715.3: Raag Todi, Ghar 4, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The mind longs for the Lord's beautiful love, (but) love for the Lord does not come by talk. I went searching for the sight (of him), looking in lane after lane; meeting the Guru, I have cast off (my) doubt. This understanding I received from the Saadh (the Guru): the writ was written on (my) forehead from the beginning. In this way, Nanak has beheld the Lord with (his own) eyes. ॥2॥
715.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The foolish heart is crazed with pride; this heart the Maya of the Great King (the Lord) has caught in attachment, like a fish (on the hook). It ever wants more, more and more; (yet) without its due, where (could it) obtain it? (The body) is the Great King's (gift), and with that (the fool) is infatuated; the luckless one has joined himself to the fire (of craving). Listen, O mind, to the teaching of all the holy ones, and all your sins will be wiped away. The one who has his due from the Great King's store, O servant Nanak, does not fall into the womb (again). ॥2॥

This shabad is in the speech of Rajasthan (Marwari): ri, ro of; thare your; gahilaro crazed; dihar fish; kaithai from where; gaath the body; lahna the share written in one's lot; gaathri the bundle, the store.
716.1: Raag Todi, Ghar 5, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Such a kindness has my dear God done (me): the five faults and the disease of ego, all these he has driven out of this body. Breaking (my) bonds and freeing (me) from Maya, he has given the Guru's Shabad (the Word) to my heart. He did not weigh my beauty or my lack of it at all; he has held me in love, (and I am) soaked in the Lord's colour. I have seen the Beloved, the curtains between (us) removed; there is bliss in (my) mind, I rejoice and am content. The house is his alone, he alone is God; that one is Nanak's Master, and to him alone (Nanak) is subject. ॥2॥
716.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, (such is) the love of my mind: these alone are (my) rites and religion, this (my) chanting; the Name of Ram is the pure way. The support of my breath, the wealth of my life, is to behold the sight of God every day. On the road and at the ford, (this) is the provision with me; I have made the Lord the friend of my mind. By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), (my) mind has become pure; in his grace (the Lord) has made (me) his own. Remembering (him) again and again, Nanak has found peace; (he is) the friend of the devotees from the beginning and through the ages. ॥2॥
716.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O dear God, my life, meet (me). Do not leave my heart even for an instant; grant your devotee this perfect gift. Dispel (my) doubt and keep (me), my Beloved, Searcher of hearts, beautiful and all-wise. The wealth of the Name is (to me) millions of kingdoms; O God, cast your glance of Amrit on my mind. May (my) tongue sing (your) praises at all hours; may (my) ears be filled and sated with (your) praise, O All-powerful. (I have come to) your shelter, O Giver of (all) beings; for ever and ever Nanak is a sacrifice (to you). ॥2॥
716.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O God, (I long for) the dust of your feet. O Lord kind to the lowly, Beloved, Enticer of the mind, in your grace fulfil my longing. Your praise pervades the ten directions; O Searcher of hearts, (you are) ever present. Those who sing your praise, O Creator, never die pining in grief. Their entanglements and bonds of Maya are destroyed; in the company of the holy (their) sorrows are wiped away. The comforts, riches and pleasures of this soul: without the Lord, O Nanak, (they) have known (them) to be false. ॥2॥
716.5: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, (such is) the thirst of my mind: I cannot live a moment without the Beloved; (my) mind holds the hope of beholding (his) sight. I remember the Name of the Immaculate Creator, and all sins of mind and body are destroyed, (the Name) of the Perfect Supreme Lord, the Giver of peace, the Imperishable, whose praise is spotless. By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), my wishes are fulfilled; in his grace the Treasure of virtues has met (me). Peace, Sahaj and comfort have welled up in the mind; (in) Nanak (shines) the light of millions of suns. ॥2॥
717.1: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord, Har Har, is the Purifier of sinners, the Giver of life, breath, honour and peace, the Searcher of hearts, dear to the mind. Beautiful, wise and clever, the Knower of all, he dwells in the hearts of (his) servants; the devotees sing (his) praises. Pure of form, peerless is the Master; in the field of deeds, what one sows, that one eats. Wonder upon wonder, (I) am struck with wonder; there is no other, no second, to set beside (him). Remembering (his) praise with the tongue again and again, I live; Nanak, (his) servant, is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
717.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, Maya is a deception: without meditating on Gobind, (it is) a fire of straw, the shade of a cloud, the water of a flood. Give up cleverness and much cunning; with both palms joined, walk on the path of the Saadh (the holy one). Remember the Master, the Searcher of hearts: this is the highest fruit of the human body. The holy ones expound the Vedas, (but) the luckless fool does not understand. O Nanak, the Lord's servants are absorbed in loving devotion; by the Simran of the Lord the wrestlers (lust and the rest) are burnt up. ॥2॥
717.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, sweet are the Guru's feet. By great fortune the Supreme God grants (them); seeing the sight of the Guru, the reward of millions (of good deeds is gained). Singing the praises of the Infallible, Imperishable (Lord), lust, anger and stubborn pride are destroyed. (Those) dyed in the love of the True One have become steady; they are not ground again in birth and death. All the delights and pleasures there are without the Lord's meditation, the merciful Sants have known to be false. Servant Nanak has found the jewel of the Name; those without the Name have all departed robbed. ॥2॥
717.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the Saadh Sangat I have remembered the Name of the Lord, Har Har; in Sahaj there is bliss day and night: a good sprout (of fortune) has come up in me. By great fortune I have met the Perfect Guru, whose end and bounds are not (to be found). Taking (him) by the hand, (he) has pulled his servant out of the poisonous ocean of the world. Through the Guru's words birth and death are cut away, and (I come) no more to the door of suffering. Nanak has grasped the shelter of the Master, and bows (to him) again and again. ॥2॥
717.5: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, (such is) the peace of my mind: (it is as if it) enjoys millions of joys and the pleasure of kingship; remembering the Lord, all pain is destroyed. The sins of millions of births are destroyed; remembering (him), body and mind are made pure, (and there is) peace. Seeing (his) form, (my) hope is fulfilled; meeting (his) sight, (my) hunger is gone. The four great gifts (padaarath), the eight great siddhis, the Kamdhenu and the Paarjat tree: (all these are) the Lord, Har Har. Nanak has grasped the shelter of the Ocean of peace; birth and death, and the womb, no more torment (him). ॥2॥

The four padaarath: dharam (righteousness), arth (wealth), kaam (fulfilment of desire) and mokh (liberation), held to be the four aims of life. The eight great siddhis: the miraculous powers of yoga (anima, laghima and the rest). Kamdhenu (dhenu, cow): the cow of heaven in the Puranas, held to grant whatever is asked of her. The Paarjat (Parijata) is a tree of Indra's heaven which, in the Puranas, rose from the churning of the ocean and grants every wish.
718.1: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (I) have enshrined the feet of the Lord, Har Har, in (my) heart. Remembering the Master, my own True Guru, my tasks have been fulfilled. Merit, charity and the worship of the Supreme God are the Lord's praise: this is the essence, reflected upon. Singing the praises of the Master, unreachable and limitless, (I) have found peace beyond measure. Those servants whom the Supreme Lord has made his own, he does not weigh their (deeds) again. Hearing the jewel of the Name and repeating it again and again, I live; the Lord is (strung) about Nanak's neck. ॥2॥
718.2: Raag Todi, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. How much can I tell of my own baseness? (I am) caught up in the relish of gold and of women, and have not sung the praise of God. Taking the false world to be true, I have formed a liking for it. Never have I remembered the Kin of the meek, who would be my companion and helper. Night and day I have stayed absorbed in Maya, and the scum of the mind has not gone. Says Nanak, now there is no salvation elsewhere, without the shelter of the Lord. ॥2॥
718.3: Raag Todi, the hymns of the Bhagats. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Some say (he is) near, some say (he is) far; (as well say) the fish of the water climbs the date palm. Why, O brother, have you taken up this idle wrangling? The one who has found the Lord has kept himself hidden. Having become a pandit, (one) expounds the Veda; the fool Namdev knows only Ram. Whose stain has remained the moment he takes the Name of Ram? Sinners become pure the moment they utter Ram. Through (his union) with Ram, servant Namdev has come to faith: the Ekadasi fast is left behind; why should (I) go to places of pilgrimage? Says Namdev, (they) have become of good deeds and good understanding; uttering Ram through the Guru's teaching, who has not gone to Baikunth (heaven)? ॥2॥
On Ekadasi, the eleventh day of the moon's fortnight, many Hindus fast from grain.
718.4: (This world) is a play of the three natures (the three qualities). In the potter's house there is the pot, in the king's house the she-camel; in the Brahmin's house there is the almanac: almanac, she-camel, pot. In the grocer's house there is asafoetida, on the buffalo's forehead the horn; in the temple there is the lingam (the emblem of Shiva): lingam, horn, asafoetida. In the oilman's house there is oil, in the forest the creepers; in the gardener's house the banana: banana, creeper, oil. Among the Sants there is Gobind, in Gokul there is Shyam; in Nama there is Ram: Ram, Shyam, Gobind. ॥4॥

The three qualities (gunas) of Maya: rajas, sattva and tamas. Go at the end of the lines is a sung word of the measure; it is not rendered. Gokul: the village where Krishna grew up; Shyam (the dark one): a name of Krishna.

711.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Todi, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Without the Lord my mind cannot live.
When the Guru unites (me) with the Lord God, my beloved, my breath of life, there is no more going round in the world-ocean.
A longing for God has taken hold of my heart, that with my eyes I may behold the Lord, the Lord God.
The merciful True Guru has made the Lord's Name firm (within me): (the Name of) the Lord is the level road to the Lord God.
I have found the Name of God, the Lord of countless hues, the Name of the Lord Govind, the Lord God;
the Lord has come to taste sweet in my heart, my mind and my body; a good fortune (shines) on my face and forehead.
Those whose minds cling to greed and the vices have forgotten the Lord, the Being most good;
they are called manmukhs (the self-willed), foolish and ignorant, and an evil fortune is on their foreheads.
From the True Guru (I) have received an intellect that discerns, the Guru's wisdom, which is of God, the Great.
Servant Nanak has received the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) from the Guru: the fortune written on (his) forehead from the beginning (has come to light). ॥4॥
711.2: Raag Todi, Ghar 1, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Sants have known no one else;
carefree, they stay ever in the Lord's love, they whose side the Master takes.
High is your canopy, O Master; no one else has spread (one like it).
Such an undying (Lord) have the devotees found; the wise remain absorbed in (his) love.
Disease and grief, pain, old age and death do not come near the Lord's servant.
They remain fearless, their attention on the One; O Nanak, (their) mind has come to rest in the Lord. ॥2॥
711.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Forgetting the Lord, there is ever ruin.
How can deception touch the one who has your shelter?
Whatever life is lived without Simran (remembrance of God) is a burning, like the long life of a snake.
Though (one) reign over the nine regions (of the world), at the last he will depart a loser.
The praises of the treasure of virtues have been sung only by the one on whom (he) has shown his grace;
that one is at peace, blessed is his birth; Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥2॥
712.1: Raag Todi, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O mind, (the mortal) has run about, run off in the ten directions,
absorbed in Maya, lured by its taste and by greed: God himself has led (him) astray.
Not for a moment has he fixed this mind on the Lord's story, the Lord's praise, the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy);
he delights at the sight of the safflower's colour, and goes off to peer into others' homes.
He has not loved the lotus feet, nor won the favour of the True Being (the Guru);
(such ones) run in many ways after what is running away, as the oilman's ox is driven round and round.
He has not practised the Naam, giving and bathing, nor sung (the Lord's) praise for an instant;
attaching (it) to many falsehoods, he has kept the mind pleased, and has not understood what is (truly) his own.
He has never done good to others, nor served the True Guru and meditated (on the Lord);
mixing with the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride), in their company and their talk, he is drunk on the wine of Maya.
I make my prayer in the Saadh Sangat: hearing (that you are) the Lord who loves devotion, I have come.
Nanak has run to the Lord's shelter: keep (my) honour, making (me) your own. ॥5॥
712.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Without understanding, the human being has come (into the world) in vain.
He makes many adornments and decorations, like a corpse being dressed.
The miser has run and run and toiled, and gathered Maya;
(with it) no giving, no merit, no service of the Sants: it has been of no use at all.
Putting on her jewels, the woman decked the bed and made a fine display;
(but) she did not gain her husband's company, and looking (at it all) again and again she was in pain.
All day long he works for hire, pounding husks with a pestle;
toil is all he gets, like one doing forced labour: it is of no use to his own home.
The one on whom God's grace has come has made the Naam dwell in his heart;
he has taken the shelter of the Saadh Sangat; O servant Nanak, he has found the Lord's sweet essence. ॥4॥
712.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O treasure of mercy, O Lord, dwell in (my) heart always.
Kindle in (me) such understanding that love for God may take hold (of me).
May I obtain the dust (of the feet) of your servant, and taking it again and again, apply it to my forehead.
(By it) one is made pure from being a great sinner; (may) I sing the Lord's Kirtan (songs of God's praise) and his virtues.
May your command taste sweet to me; may what you do please me.
Whatever you give, with that may this (mind) be satisfied; may I run nowhere else.
May I know you, God, my Master, ever near; one should live as the dust of all.
When the company of the holy is gained, then one finds one's own God.
For ever and ever we are your little ones; you, God, are our sovereign.
Nanak is (your) child, you are (his) mother and father; your Name in (his) mouth is (his) milk. ॥4॥
713.1: Raag Todi, Ghar 2, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I beg the gift of the Name, O Master.
Nothing else will go with me; (may I) by your grace receive the singing of your praises.
Rule, riches and many pleasures and delights: all are the shade of a tree.
Running and running, (the mortal) runs about in many ways, (yet) all his deeds are of no avail.
If I want anything else but Govind, all (of it) is seen to be unripe.
Says Nanak, I beg the dust (of the feet) of the Sants, (so that) my mind may find rest. ॥2॥
713.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Name of dear God is the support of the mind.
It is the life, the breath and the peace of this mind; it is what I have to live by.
The Naam is (my) caste, the Naam is my honour, the Naam is my family.
The Naam is a companion, ever at my side; the Lord's Name carries me across.
Pleasures of the senses are spoken of as many, (yet) none of them goes along.
The Naam is Nanak's beloved friend; what lies in my treasury is the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
713.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sing the sublime praises (of the Lord), and the diseases are wiped away;
the face becomes bright, the mind becomes pure, and your world here and hereafter is kept safe.
Washing (his) feet, I serve the Guru, and offer my mind (to him) as the offering.
Give up selfhood, strife and pride, and accept whatever comes to be.
He alone is set to the service of the Sants on whose forehead (that) writ is written.
Says Nanak, apart from the One there is no other able to do (anything). ॥2॥
713.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O True Guru, I have come to your shelter.
May I receive peace, the Lord's Name and honour; take away my anxiety.
No other resting place comes to mind; worn out, I have fallen at your door.
Set aside the account (of my deeds); only without an account can we be freed; save us, the worthless.
Ever forgiving, ever merciful, (he) gives support to all.
Servant Nanak has taken the shelter of the Sant (the Guru): save (me) this time. ॥2॥
713.5: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Singing with the tongue the praises of Gopal, the treasure (of virtues),
peace, Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and joy well up in the mind, and all sorrows flee.
Whatever they ask for, that very thing they receive, serving the feet of the Lord, the home of every delight;
they are freed from both birth and death, and cross the terrifying world-ocean.
Searching and searching, the servants have reflected on the essence, and hold to Govind alone.
If you want lasting well-being, O Nanak, remember Narayan for ever. ॥2॥
714.1: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By the Guru's grace the slanderer has been driven off.
The Supreme Lord God became merciful, and with the arrow of Shiv (the Lord, the source of good) cut off (his) head.
Death, its net and Jam (the messenger of Death) cannot (even) look at (me): (I) have taken the path of Truth.
Eating and spending, nothing runs short: (I) have earned the wealth of the jewel of (the Name of) Ram.
Within an instant (the slanderer) turned to ashes: he reaped what he himself had done.
Servant Nanak speaks (the word of) the scriptures, Agam and Nigam; all the world sees it all. ॥2॥
714.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O miser, (your) body and mind are full of sins.
In the Saadh Sangat meditate on the Master: the One Lord alone (can) cover (them).
The ship has many holes bursting open, and they cannot be stopped (by hand).
(If one) worships the One whose ship it is, in his company the counterfeit become genuine.
(The mortal) wants to lift mountains with talk, (but) they stay lying where they are.
Nanak has neither strength nor any power; O God, keep (us): we have fallen at your shelter. ॥2॥
714.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In my mind I meditate on the lotus feet of the Lord.
The Lord's Name is the medicine: an axe that cuts out (the ills of) bile and wind and destroys them.
(It) dispels the three fevers, destroys pain, and is a store of peace.
No obstacle touches the one whose prayer is before God.
By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), Narayan is the physician, God the One, the Cause of causes.
(To those of) a child's mind (he) is the perfect Giver of peace; Nanak's support is the Lord, Har Har. ॥2॥
714.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, for ever and ever.
Showing his grace, the Master, the Supreme Lord, has himself made (the heart's deserted town) inhabited again.
He whose (servants) they were has himself taken care of them again, and sorrow and anguish have perished.
Giving his hand, (he) has protected his servants; the Lord has become (their) mother and father.
Every being and creature has become kind, (since) the Lord, the Master, has shown mercy.
Nanak has fallen at the shelter of the Destroyer of pain, whose glory is great. ॥2॥
714.5: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Master, I have come to your shelter, to your court.
O Giver who destroys millions of offences, who but you can save (me)?
Searching and searching in many ways, I have reflected on all things:
in the Saadh Sangat the supreme state is attained; caught up in Maya, in its bonds, (people) lose (the game of life).
Love for the lotus feet has taken hold of (my) mind, (since) the beloved godly ones have met (me).
Nanak rejoices, repeating the Lord (again and again), and has rid (himself) of all diseases. ॥2॥
715.1: Raag Todi, Ghar 3, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Yes, yes, O fool, you are clinging (to it), and not a little;
what is not yours, that you have taken for your own.
You have not recognised your own Ram for even an instant;
what is another's, that you have believed to be yours.
The Naam is (your) companion: that you have not made to dwell in the mind;
you have fixed your attention on what will leave (you).
You have hoarded that by which (you stay) hungry and thirsty;
the Amrit (life-giving) Naam you have not taken as provisions (for the journey).
(You) have fallen into the well of lust, anger and attachment;
by the Guru's grace, O Nanak, (only) some rare one has crossed over. ॥4॥
715.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Within me there is the One alone, the Lord, the Lord;
I have made acquaintance with no other.
By great fortune I have found my Guru;
the Guru has made the Lord's Name firm within me.
The Lord, Har Har, is (my) chanting and austerity, (my) fasts and observances;
meditating on the Lord, Har Har, (I have) every comfort and well-being.
(My) conduct, (my) dealings and (my) caste are the Lord's praises;
hearing the Lord's Kirtan, (there is) supreme bliss.
Says Nanak, the one who has found the Master:
everything has come into his house. ॥4॥
715.3: Raag Todi, Ghar 4, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The mind longs for the Lord's beautiful love,
(but) love for the Lord does not come by talk.
I went searching for the sight (of him), looking in lane after lane;
meeting the Guru, I have cast off (my) doubt.
This understanding I received from the Saadh (the Guru): the writ was written on (my) forehead from the beginning.
In this way, Nanak has beheld the Lord with (his own) eyes. ॥2॥
715.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The foolish heart is crazed with pride;
this heart the Maya of the Great King (the Lord)
has caught in attachment, like a fish (on the hook).
It ever wants more, more and more; (yet) without its due, where (could it) obtain it?
(The body) is the Great King's (gift), and with that (the fool) is infatuated; the luckless one has joined himself to the fire (of craving).
Listen, O mind, to the teaching of all the holy ones, and all your sins will be wiped away.
The one who has his due from the Great King's store, O servant Nanak, does not fall into the womb (again). ॥2॥
716.1: Raag Todi, Ghar 5, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Such a kindness has my dear God done (me):
the five faults and the disease of ego, all these he has driven out of this body.
Breaking (my) bonds and freeing (me) from Maya, he has given the Guru's Shabad (the Word) to my heart.
He did not weigh my beauty or my lack of it at all; he has held me in love, (and I am) soaked in the Lord's colour.
I have seen the Beloved, the curtains between (us) removed; there is bliss in (my) mind, I rejoice and am content.
The house is his alone, he alone is God; that one is Nanak's Master, and to him alone (Nanak) is subject. ॥2॥
716.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, (such is) the love of my mind:
these alone are (my) rites and religion, this (my) chanting; the Name of Ram is the pure way.
The support of my breath, the wealth of my life, is to behold the sight of God every day.
On the road and at the ford, (this) is the provision with me; I have made the Lord the friend of my mind.
By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), (my) mind has become pure; in his grace (the Lord) has made (me) his own.
Remembering (him) again and again, Nanak has found peace; (he is) the friend of the devotees from the beginning and through the ages. ॥2॥
716.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O dear God, my life, meet (me).
Do not leave my heart even for an instant; grant your devotee this perfect gift.
Dispel (my) doubt and keep (me), my Beloved, Searcher of hearts, beautiful and all-wise.
The wealth of the Name is (to me) millions of kingdoms; O God, cast your glance of Amrit on my mind.
May (my) tongue sing (your) praises at all hours; may (my) ears be filled and sated with (your) praise, O All-powerful.
(I have come to) your shelter, O Giver of (all) beings; for ever and ever Nanak is a sacrifice (to you). ॥2॥
716.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O God, (I long for) the dust of your feet.
O Lord kind to the lowly, Beloved, Enticer of the mind, in your grace fulfil my longing.
Your praise pervades the ten directions; O Searcher of hearts, (you are) ever present.
Those who sing your praise, O Creator, never die pining in grief.
Their entanglements and bonds of Maya are destroyed; in the company of the holy (their) sorrows are wiped away.
The comforts, riches and pleasures of this soul: without the Lord, O Nanak, (they) have known (them) to be false. ॥2॥
716.5: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, (such is) the thirst of my mind:
I cannot live a moment without the Beloved; (my) mind holds the hope of beholding (his) sight.
I remember the Name of the Immaculate Creator, and all sins of mind and body are destroyed,
(the Name) of the Perfect Supreme Lord, the Giver of peace, the Imperishable, whose praise is spotless.
By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), my wishes are fulfilled; in his grace the Treasure of virtues has met (me).
Peace, Sahaj and comfort have welled up in the mind; (in) Nanak (shines) the light of millions of suns. ॥2॥
717.1: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord, Har Har, is the Purifier of sinners,
the Giver of life, breath, honour and peace, the Searcher of hearts, dear to the mind.
Beautiful, wise and clever, the Knower of all, he dwells in the hearts of (his) servants; the devotees sing (his) praises.
Pure of form, peerless is the Master; in the field of deeds, what one sows, that one eats.
Wonder upon wonder, (I) am struck with wonder; there is no other, no second, to set beside (him).
Remembering (his) praise with the tongue again and again, I live; Nanak, (his) servant, is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
717.2: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, Maya is a deception:
without meditating on Gobind, (it is) a fire of straw, the shade of a cloud, the water of a flood.
Give up cleverness and much cunning; with both palms joined, walk on the path of the Saadh (the holy one).
Remember the Master, the Searcher of hearts: this is the highest fruit of the human body.
The holy ones expound the Vedas, (but) the luckless fool does not understand.
O Nanak, the Lord's servants are absorbed in loving devotion; by the Simran of the Lord the wrestlers (lust and the rest) are burnt up. ॥2॥
717.3: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, sweet are the Guru's feet.
By great fortune the Supreme God grants (them); seeing the sight of the Guru, the reward of millions (of good deeds is gained).
Singing the praises of the Infallible, Imperishable (Lord), lust, anger and stubborn pride are destroyed.
(Those) dyed in the love of the True One have become steady; they are not ground again in birth and death.
All the delights and pleasures there are without the Lord's meditation, the merciful Sants have known to be false.
Servant Nanak has found the jewel of the Name; those without the Name have all departed robbed. ॥2॥
717.4: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the Saadh Sangat I have remembered the Name of the Lord, Har Har;
in Sahaj there is bliss day and night: a good sprout (of fortune) has come up in me.
By great fortune I have met the Perfect Guru, whose end and bounds are not (to be found).
Taking (him) by the hand, (he) has pulled his servant out of the poisonous ocean of the world.
Through the Guru's words birth and death are cut away, and (I come) no more to the door of suffering.
Nanak has grasped the shelter of the Master, and bows (to him) again and again. ॥2॥
717.5: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, (such is) the peace of my mind:
(it is as if it) enjoys millions of joys and the pleasure of kingship; remembering the Lord, all pain is destroyed.
The sins of millions of births are destroyed; remembering (him), body and mind are made pure, (and there is) peace.
Seeing (his) form, (my) hope is fulfilled; meeting (his) sight, (my) hunger is gone.
The four great gifts (padaarath), the eight great siddhis, the Kamdhenu and the Paarjat tree: (all these are) the Lord, Har Har.
Nanak has grasped the shelter of the Ocean of peace; birth and death, and the womb, no more torment (him). ॥2॥
718.1: Raag Todi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(I) have enshrined the feet of the Lord, Har Har, in (my) heart.
Remembering the Master, my own True Guru, my tasks have been fulfilled.
Merit, charity and the worship of the Supreme God are the Lord's praise: this is the essence, reflected upon.
Singing the praises of the Master, unreachable and limitless, (I) have found peace beyond measure.
Those servants whom the Supreme Lord has made his own, he does not weigh their (deeds) again.
Hearing the jewel of the Name and repeating it again and again, I live; the Lord is (strung) about Nanak's neck. ॥2॥
718.2: Raag Todi, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
How much can I tell of my own baseness?
(I am) caught up in the relish of gold and of women, and have not sung the praise of God.
Taking the false world to be true, I have formed a liking for it.
Never have I remembered the Kin of the meek, who would be my companion and helper.
Night and day I have stayed absorbed in Maya, and the scum of the mind has not gone.
Says Nanak, now there is no salvation elsewhere, without the shelter of the Lord. ॥2॥
718.3: Raag Todi, the hymns of the Bhagats.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Some say (he is) near, some say (he is) far;
(as well say) the fish of the water climbs the date palm.
Why, O brother, have you taken up this idle wrangling?
The one who has found the Lord has kept himself hidden.
Having become a pandit, (one) expounds the Veda;
the fool Namdev knows only Ram.
Whose stain has remained the moment he takes the Name of Ram?
Sinners become pure the moment they utter Ram.
Through (his union) with Ram, servant Namdev has come to faith:
the Ekadasi fast is left behind; why should (I) go to places of pilgrimage?
Says Namdev, (they) have become of good deeds and good understanding;
uttering Ram through the Guru's teaching, who has not gone to Baikunth (heaven)? ॥2॥
718.4: (This world) is a play of the three natures (the three qualities).
In the potter's house there is the pot, in the king's house the she-camel;
in the Brahmin's house there is the almanac: almanac, she-camel, pot.
In the grocer's house there is asafoetida, on the buffalo's forehead the horn;
in the temple there is the lingam (the emblem of Shiva): lingam, horn, asafoetida.
In the oilman's house there is oil, in the forest the creepers;
in the gardener's house the banana: banana, creeper, oil.
Among the Sants there is Gobind, in Gokul there is Shyam;
in Nama there is Ram: Ram, Shyam, Gobind. ॥4॥
